intervals.label: hosting the CHOOZ neutrino experiment (reactor-neutrino site)
intervals.locator: EPJ C 27, 331 (2003) = hep-ex/0301017, section on data taking
intervals.note: Start is the first day of CHOOZ data taking, the earliest dated use of the site; the underground laboratory itself must be older and its construction date was not sourced. Left open because the site went on to host Double Chooz (from 2011 on this record's other interval) and no source says it closed; the idle years 1998-2011 are not documented.
intervals.quote: The data acquisition period extended over 450 days, from 12 March 1997 till 20 July 1998

intervals.label: hosting Double Chooz
intervals.note: Lower bound: April 2011 is the first Double Chooz data taking at the site (far detector in the existing CHOOZ laboratory), so hosting began no later than this; no official facility page was reachable (checked 2026-09-17) to source an earlier founding or operating date. The site remains a candidate host for other reactor-neutrino work (e.g. NUCLEUS) beyond Double Chooz's own end of data taking in 2017, so the interval is left open-ended.
intervals.quote: Since the far detector could be installed in the existing laboratory of the original CHOOZ experiment [9], its data taking started first, in April 2011.

name: Chooz Reactor Neutrino Site
notes: The Double Chooz official site (double-chooz.fr, doublechooz.in2p3.fr, chooz.in2p3.fr) was unreachable (DNS failure on every domain tried, checked 2026-09-17); this record relies on the 2012 arXiv discovery paper, the collaboration's 2022 detector paper, and INSPIRE.
experiment:nucleus also uses this facility as its host site.

operator.note: No source consulted (checked 2026-10-28) states an explicit operator of the experimental site distinct from the Double Chooz Collaboration and EDF; the collaboration's detector paper names EDF only as operator of the Chooz-B nuclear power plant next to the site.
operator.quote: two almost identical detectors located at the Chooz-B nuclear power plant operated by the EDF company

summary.plain: The site near the Chooz nuclear power station in northern France where the Double Chooz experiment placed two detectors to catch antineutrinos from the reactors.
summary.technical: Reactor-neutrino site adjacent to the Chooz-B nuclear power plant, Ardennes, France, hosting the Double Chooz near (400 m) and far (1050 m) detector halls.
